name: realism-track-v2
purpose: scientific-quality evolution track for the SIMULATOR (not for trading strategies): candidate configurations are judged on several objectives at once and kept in a Pareto archive. The track can conclude 'not an improvement'.
targets: historical BTCUSDT 1m TRAIN days only (2026-09-01..05), 60-minute windows, median and IQR per fact (evolutionx.evaluation.calibration.window_targets('train')). Validation/held-out calibration days are NOT used: they were already exposed in the v0.1 calibration and would not be independent.
estimator: same multi_facts() estimator for historical windows and for each simulated 3600 s run (1m closes from the venue-0 mid)
candidate_space: a candidate is ONLY a dict of SimConfig overrides restricted to allowed_fields; it cannot supply code, targets, objectives, seeds or duration
verdict_rule: paired by seed against EACH incumbent listed in 'incumbents'. 'improvement' = no objective worse (t-interval of paired diff not entirely above 0 for any error objective) AND at least one error objective better (t-interval entirely below 0); 'trade-off' = some objective better and some worse; 'not an improvement' = otherwise. Cost counts only if the mean differs by more than the cost tolerance.
archive_rule: a candidate enters the Pareto archive if no archived entry dominates it (tolerance above) and it is not a behavioural duplicate; entries it dominates move to history with dominated_by. The archive stores the sha256 of this file and refuses to update if the rules change.

why: v1 archive admitted/evicted behaviourally IDENTICAL configurations on CPU-time noise alone (R_leveraged_size_0.5 had the same run fingerprints as realistic_fundamental and evicted it by being 13% faster)
that duplicate exposed a silent no-op knob: size_scale['leveraged'] (leveraged agents have no order-size parameter); now rejected by build_population
v1 compared every variant only with the default config, whose exogenous fundamental is mis-specified, so every variant looked like an improvement

dominance.rule: a dominates b if a <= b*(1+tol) on every objective and a < b*(1-tol) on at least one (mean over seeds)

duplicate_rule: a candidate whose run fingerprints equal those of an archived entry is a behavioural duplicate and is not admitted
